subject: SLA exemption request and rollback playbook for content-filter / tool-call structured-output failures
messages:
From: Anita Patel <anita.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA exception request: content filter & tool calls causing structured-output failures

Hi Tessa,

We're seeing a spike in structured-output failures in our integration with Redwood since the 2026-07-12 runtime update. The failures are tied to the content-filter layer hitting heuristic matches, which in turn causes downstream tool-call payloads to be truncated or mis-mapped in our analytics pipeline. Impact: several hourly jobs failed to materialize final JSON blobs (roughly 0.6% of requests last 48h), which breaks our ingestion and downstream reconciliation.

We've attached a sample failure bundle and an impact CSV. Given that our renewal is scheduled for Aug 3, we need an expedited carve-out request that covers:
- temporary SLA tolerance for structured-output completeness for the affected routes,
- a rollback/canary plan so we can avoid a production regression for the next two weeks, and
- confirmation on whether Redwood will provide credits if the degradation exceeds the threshold in the standard SLA.

Can you please advise the internal process and expected timeline for approval? We need a firm plan by EOD Friday 2026-07-16 to inform our procurement and execs.

Thanks,
Anita Patel
Director, Integrations — Acme Health

Attachments: failure-sample.json (sample request/response), impact-metrics.csv (hourly counts)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Patel <anita.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exception request: content filter & tool calls causing structured-output failures

Hi Anita — thanks for the samples and the clear ask. We're prioritizing this.

Next steps from our side:
1) I've routed to eng + security (cc'd). Neha, can you confirm repro scope and whether this is strictly content-filter heuristic behavior vs a model-output regression?
2) Karthik, I'll need a commercial steer: Acme's timeline is tight; do we have precedent for short-term credits while we fix a filtering config?
3) We'll send a proposed roll-forward/rollback playbook and an exemption request form (for your signature).

We aim to provide a mitigation proposal by EOD Thu 2026-07-15 and a final decision Friday 2026-07-16. If that timeline needs compression, say so now and we'll escalate.

Tessa
Senior Manager, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Anita / Tessa — quick commercial note:
- For renewals we typically consider a temporary SLA carve-out paired with a one-time credit when the root cause is behaviorally expected (e.g., content-filter heuristics updated to be more conservative).
- Proposal: approve a scoped exemption that excludes structured-output completeness for the specific API routes listed in your impact CSV for a period no longer than 21 days, contingent on an agreed remediation plan and a canary rollback option.
- I'll draft the credit amount range and attach a short MOU for signature.

I've attached an initial draft SLA-exemption MOU (sla-exemption-draft.docx). If legal from Acme is comfortable, we can fast-track. Karthik

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Anita Patel <anita.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exemption request: proposed technical mitigation and rollback playbook

Hi all — short technical summary and actionable playbook attached. Key points:
- Root cause: the updated content-filter ruleset increased false-positive matches on nested JSON keys used by Acme's tool-calls (filters apply prior to serializer normalization). Not a model architecture regression.
- Mitigation (immediate): route your critical routes to the non-filtered model-variant (model-variant: rwd-2.9-no-filter) via our routing policy. This preserves structured output while we tune filters. Expected lift: >98% completeness in the first hour after reroute.
- Canary / rollback playbook (canary_playbook.md attached):
  * Canary window: 4 hours in a US-east region, 1% traffic, monitor structured-output completeness and token latency at 1-min granularity.
  * Automatic rollback triggers: structured-output completeness < 95% OR 99th-percentile token latency increase > 40ms over baseline for the canary window.
  * Fallback: if the canary fails, auto-route to rwd-2.7-stable for affected routes and enable prefix KV cache bypass for those requests.

We recommend a scoped carve-out for 14 days while we complete filter tuning and regression tests; we will deliver a final filter configuration and test logs within that window. I've attached repro-trace-logs.txt and the canary_playbook.md.

Neha Kapoor
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: canary_playbook.md, repro-trace-logs.txt
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Patel <anita.patel@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA exemption request: content filter & tool calls — approval & next steps

Anita — thanks for the patience. Summary and next steps below (finalized):

1) Decision: Redwood approves a scoped SLA carve-out for Acme Health covering structured-output completeness for the affected API routes listed in your impact CSV. Scope: 14 days starting when you sign the exemption_request_form.pdf.
2) Credit: a one-time usage credit will be applied if your measured structured-output completeness drops below 94% for more than 3 hours within the exemption window. Karthik will follow up with the exact credit calculation.
3) Technical path: Neha's mitigation plan is approved. Immediate action: Acme should route 1% traffic to the canary variant and confirm telemetry link. If canary passes per the triggers, we will incrementally increase traffic and finalize filter updates.
4) Rollback/Fail-safe: automatic routing to rwd-2.7-stable and cache bypass as described in the canary playbook.
5) Paperwork: signing path — I've attached exemption_request_form.pdf and a Doc link to the MOU draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Acme-SLA/requests. Please return the signed form by EOD Tue 2026-07-20 to start the exemption window.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow to walk through the canary steps and assign an on-call engineer.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: exemption_request_form.pdf
